# Installing FUSION2 {#sec-installing}

FUSION2 runs on 64-bit Windows. Each tool is a single self-contained
executable with no separate libraries to install.

## Download a release

1. Open the [FUSION2 Releases page](https://github.com/jstrunk001/FUSION2/releases)
   and download the zip file from the latest release
   (`FUSION2_tools_v<version>-<date>.zip`).
2. Unzip it into a folder of your choice, for example `C:\FUSION2`.

The folder then holds:

| Item | What it is |
|:--------|:------------------------------|
| 15 `.exe` files | The tools: `catalog`, `filterdata`, `thindata`, `groundfilter`, `clipdata`, `canopymodel`, `returndensity`, `densitymetrics`, `gridmetrics`, `cloudmetrics`, `topometrics`, `gridsurfacestats`, `canopymaxima`, `treeseg`, and `pipeline` |
| `proj_data\proj.db` | The coordinate-system database the tools use to read and write map projections |
| `FUSION2_Manual.pdf` | This manual |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | What changed in each release |

: Contents of a FUSION2 release zip. {#tbl-release-contents}

Keep `proj_data` in the same folder as the executables. The tools look for
it next to themselves. Without it, they still run, but they may not
recognize some coordinate systems and will print a warning about
`proj.db`.

## Put the tools on your PATH

Adding the folder to your `PATH` lets you run a tool by name from any
folder. In PowerShell, for the current user:

```powershell
$dir = "C:\FUSION2"
$old = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "$old;$dir", "User")
```

Open a new terminal afterwards so the change takes effect. Without this
step, run each tool by its full path (`C:\FUSION2\gridmetrics.exe`).

## Check the installation

Every tool prints its options when run with `/?`:

```bat
gridmetrics /?
```

If the options list appears, the tools are ready. @sec-tool-help collects
this help text for every tool.

## Build from source

The FUSION2 repository's `README.md` explains how to build the tools with
CMake and the `build.ps1` script, including the minimal (GeoTIFF-only) and
full-format GDAL build profiles. `build.ps1` also runs the unit tests
described in @sec-unit-tests and renders this manual.
